instrument: probe: write fact old in space A, newer in A supersedes it, promote_to_core(old) -> recall(core) serves old? (today False/False); plus a route test that promote of a closed memory answers a reason, not 404
title: Promoting a closed memory to core answers 200 and then hides it everywhere
body:
## Summary
A project's superseded memory (or retired forget marker) can be promoted to core; the route says it moved, and recall then serves it in no space at all.

## Description
`src/athena/spaces/memory.py:122` promote_to_core -> `Brain.unstamp` (src/athena/core/brain/store.py) moves any fact/procedural of the space, including one a same-space successor closes in `companion_supersede`. The project memory page query (`src/athena/spaces/memory.py` `n.space = ? AND n.kind IN`) lists closed memories and forget markers, so the button is reachable. After the move a core memory is closed by a project memory: `NOT_SUPERSEDED` (`src/athena/core/recall.py:104`) and sleep's `_LIVE` (`src/athena/core/sleep/book.py:61`) hide it in core and every project, where the successor is invisible - the case `_require_supersedable` refuses at write (ADR 0225). Promoting a forget marker also widens its bar from one project to everywhere (`book.py` bars). Fixed: unstamp refuses a memory closed by a memory of its space and a retired marker, and `src/athena/spaces/routes.py:228` answers that reason instead of 404 'not a memory of this project'; optionally the page hides closed memories. Defence in depth: the closed-memory predicate counts a closer only when it is visible in the view (technique agent-memory/decay-and-forgetting).

## Flow
- write fact old in space A; write newer in A with supersedes=[old]
- POST /spaces/A/memory/<old>/core -> 200 {kind: fact}
- recall(core, 'zephyr'): old not served, newer not served; recall(A): newer only

## Expected impact
A person who promotes a memory sees success and the memory never reaches core; measured by the probe's served flags. Could break: a caller relying on promote accepting any fact of the space.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a promote either moves a memory core can serve or says why it cannot
Before: probe (scratchpad probe_unstamp.py): promote -> 'fact'; core view old served False, new served False
After: not built - needs store.py plus the spaces route's copy (outside this round's write set)
Method: probe - reproduced on the real tree; the fix spans another context's route
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/core/brain/store.py unstamp: `if row is None or row[0] not in SUPERSEDABLE_KINDS or row[2] != space: return None` (no closed check)
src/athena/spaces/routes.py:228-229 `if moved is None: return error(404, "unknown_ref", ...)`
probe output:
promote old -> fact
'' old served: False new served: False
'spc_e2f3' old served: False new served: True

title: Promote and erase rewrite write-once memories that replication cannot carry
body:
## Summary
`Brain.unstamp` rewrites a replicated fact in place and `Brain.erase_space` deletes replicated files, but ADR 0140 replication assumes episodes, facts and procedurals are write-once; neither act reaches a paired PC.

## Description
`src/athena/peer/replicate.py:7` states 'no rewrite path exists for them in store'; ADR 0225 added two (store.py `unstamp`, `erase_space`). The pull cursor follows `created` (`src/athena/peer/replicate.py:44`) and unstamp keeps `created`, so a peer that already pulled the stamped copy never sees the promotion; one that meets both copies files a conflict (`.peer/conflicts/<id>.<peer>.md`). Erase on one PC leaves every peer holding the project's memories, and a fresh pairing or cursor reset pulls them back onto the erasing PC (invisible, the space file is gone, but on disk again). Fixed needs a design decision: promote as a new core memory that supersedes the stamped one (write-once kept) and erase as a replicated tombstone, or declare both device-local in ADR 0225. Technique: sync-replication/projection-security.

## Flow
- PC A and PC B paired, both hold fact F stamped space X
- on A: promote F -> A's file loses `space:`; B's cursor is past F.created -> B keeps F in X
- on A: erase X -> files gone on A; B still serves them; a re-pair pulls them back

## Expected impact
Anyone with two paired PCs: a promotion or an erase holds on one device only. Could break: the write-once premise every pull rule rests on.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the wall's explicit acts mean the same on every paired device
Before: walked: unstamp keeps created (store.py `UPDATE companion_node SET space = ?, content_hash = ?`); manifest pages by created_at (replicate.py manifest)
After: not measured - depends on the design chosen
Method: simulation - three cases walked (promote after pull, promote before pull, erase then re-pair); no two-brain harness built because the fix shape is a direction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
src/athena/peer/replicate.py:7 '(no rewrite path exists for them in :mod:`athena.core.brain.store`)'
src/athena/peer/replicate.py:44-47 the cursor follows created
src/athena/core/brain/store.py unstamp: self._write_file(rel, moved); UPDATE ... space, content_hash (created unchanged)
src/athena/core/brain/store.py erase_space: (self.root / rel).unlink(missing_ok=True)

title: Erasing a project leaves its memory keys in sleep journals and conflict copies
body:
## Summary
`Brain.erase_space` removes the project's episodes, facts, procedurals, rows and proposals, but sleep journals (`cycles/*.md`) still name its memories' keys and `.peer/conflicts/` copies of its memories stay on disk.

## Description
store.py `erase_space` walks only `_STAMPED_DIRS` (episodes, semantic, procedurals). The per-pass cycle report (`src/athena/core/sleep/cycle.py:252` via `Brain.write_cycle_report`) records lines like ``fact `<key>` in <space>`` (`src/athena/core/sleep/cycle.py:289`, `:400`, `:424`), indexed as `cycle_report` rows with FTS bodies. Replication conflict copies live at `brain/.peer/conflicts/<id>.<peer>.md` (`src/athena/peer/replicate.py` `_conflict`). ADR 0225 says erase takes every file and every row of the space. Fixed needs a decision: redact the space's journal lines (rewrites a history record - irreversible) or say in the erase confirmation that journals and conflict copies are kept.

## Flow
- run a sleep pass in project A that learns fact `client budget`
- erase project A
- grep brain/cycles: the key is still there; companion_fts still matches it on kind cycle_report

## Expected impact
A person who erases a project expecting its words gone finds them in the journal. Could break: the journal's role as an unedited record.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - erase leaves no searchable word of the space
Before: walked: erase's walk excludes cycles/ and .peer/
After: not measured
Method: simulation - code walk of the two writers; not probed because the remedy (rewrite history vs disclose) is a human call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
src/athena/core/brain/store.py _STAMPED_DIRS = (episodes, semantic/<scope>, procedurals/<scope>)
src/athena/core/sleep/cycle.py:289 label = f"{candidate.kind} `{_tick(candidate.key)}`{_in_space(space)}"
src/athena/core/brain/store.py erase_space FTS comment: 'must leave no searchable word of the space behind'
